subject: visual-arts

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · Component 1 Portfolio (60%) · Component 2 Externally Set Assignment (40%, 8 hours' supervised time)

note: Units follow the syllabus's own parts: the skills common to both components, then the assessment objectives as teaching stages for the Component 1 Portfolio (Record, Explore, Develop), the five areas of study, and finally the Component 2 Externally Set Assignment (Present). Atlas levels map by tier: foundational and intermediate lessons build the visual elements and recording skills, advanced and expert lessons carry the develop and present stages.

program.section: Skills and understanding common to both components
program.title: Visual language and the elements
topics: Visual language such as colour, tone, line, form, texture and composition
Understanding form, shape, texture, perspective and scale
Creating imagery with consideration for composition, space, balance and colour relationships
Recording from first-hand and secondary resources and personal research
Reflecting, refining and adapting

program.title: Record: observation and research
topics: AO1 Record: select relevant subject matter from a variety of sources
Recording from a range of primary and secondary sources such as places, people and objects
Observational study: drawing, sketching, painting, samples, prints, photography
Research into relevant artists, designers and craftspeople; museum, gallery and studio visits
Communicating intention and purpose through selected sources

program.title: Explore: media, techniques and processes
topics: AO2 Explore: select appropriate resources, media, techniques and processes
The inherent properties of media and the visual elements
Experimenting with media, techniques and processes and taking creative risks
Reviewed and refined use of media to express ideas effectively

program.title: Develop: investigation and critical understanding
topics: AO3 Develop: form personal connections between research, recording and explorations
Crafting a creative journey that demonstrates critical understanding
Exploring visual elements: alternative compositions, angles, viewpoints, perspectives, forms and designs
Reflecting on strengths and weaknesses to outline modifications
Evaluating their own work, reviewing and editing

program.title: Component 1 areas of study
topics: Painting and/or other media: painting, drawing, assemblage/collage, printmaking
Graphic communication: illustration, packaging design, advertising, typography
Three-dimensional design: sculpture/ceramics, product design, architecture, craft design, jewellery
Textiles and/or Fashion: fashion design and illustration, costume design, screen printing, batik, surface pattern
Photography
A portfolio that demonstrates progression of ideas and insights

program.title: Present: responding to a given theme
topics: AO4 Present: realise intention and understand visual language
Producing a personal response to a given theme
Focusing on a particular specialism
Supporting studies and a final outcome of 8 hours' total duration
